summary: The main article describes a visible-light/nickel-catalyzed carboxylation method using sodium formate. It includes a graphical abstract, a figure comparing catalytic strategies, a table for reaction optimization, a figure evaluating sulfonylating agents, and a table detailing the substrate scope for (hetero)aryl and vinyl bromides.

items.heading: Figure 1
items.caption: Catalytic strategies for C(sp 2 ) carboxylation.
items.description: Comparison of previous carboxylation methods using CO2 or electrochemical processes with the current work using formate activation.

items.heading: Table 1
items.caption: Optimization of reaction conditions for the carboxylation of 3-bromoanisole.
items.description: Screening of various HAT catalysts, showing that phenyl triflimide is uniquely effective for the carboxylation of electron-rich/neutral arenes.

items.heading: Figure 2
items.caption: Evaluation of alternative sulfonylating agents in place of phenyl triflimide.
items.description: Comparison of yields when using different sulfonylating agents like methanesulfonyl chloride and toluenesulfonyl chloride.

items.heading: Table 2
items.caption: Scope of Ni/Photoredox-Catalyzed Carboxylation of (Hetero)Aryl Bromides and Sodium Formate
items.description: Substrate scope showing the carboxylation of various aryl, heteroaryl, and vinyl bromides with different functional group tolerances.
